correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=5,504,798 with n=4m+r, an inverted ordered Farey pair (a/b,c/d) satisfies c/d>=(a+1)/(b-1), reducing the minimal intervening count to C_n(a,b). The published Wang-Xie-Zhao uniform bound gives C>U(n) when b<=n/4 or b-2a outside {1,2}; its explicit error E(n)<n/36-4 was independently checked numerically at the stated cutoff (positive margin 0.01549...). Remaining coprime starts have nested I_t, J_t, K_t intervals. For nonterminal I/J/K families, the proof lists additional reduced fractions strictly in the corresponding intervals, increasing the known lower U(n); r=3 exceptional K_m requires an actual inverted right endpoint beyond the non-coprime immediate candidate and gains extra m/(2m-1). The sole surviving I_m for r=0 or J_m for r=1,2,3 has the known reduced right endpoint; a later endpoint adds at least one interior Farey term. Consequently exactly one minimizing ordered pair at each n in scope, with known f(n) values m+1,m+2,m+2,m+4. Independent brute exact Farey sample n=120..123 and n=144 found only the canonical pair; finite checks do not establish the cutoff theorem.
